text.title: Incident Comms Templates Internal External Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for the `IncidentCommsBundle`: the severity x audience matrix with first-post deadlines, update intervals and the post-incident email deadline; the four templates (status page, customer email, exec brief, internal channel) with their token list and `last_drilled` dates; and, per live incident, the filled updates with lifecycle state, timestamp, impact and next-update time, the external-review flags that keep speculation and internal names out, the internal post with a named commander, the five-field exec brief, and the Resolved message with its postmortem commitment. Validator: `scripts/validate-incident-comms-templates-internal-external.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the validator's cross-field block checks beyond the schema: the highest severity row (lowest P / SEV number) lists `status_page` (r-severity-audience-matrix); every double-brace token in a template body is in `token_list` (r-placeholders-resolved-before-send); per incident, the matrix has a row for its severity, `audiences_sent` equals that row's audiences, the first external update is inside `first_post_deadline_minutes`, and no gap between consecutive status-page updates exceeds `update_interval_minutes` (r-severity-audience-matrix, r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence); status-page states never move backwards through Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved (r-status-page-lifecycle-states); `internal_post.severity` equals the incident's, and an `exec_brief` is present whenever the matrix row lists `exec_brief` (r-internal-post-fields, r-exec-brief-one-screen); when a status-page update is Resolved, `resolved` is present with `end_at` after `start_at`, `postmortem_due` after `end_at`, and `post_incident_email_sent_at` at most `post_incident_email_deadline_hours` after `end_at` when set (r-resolution-and-postmortem-commitment); every template used for an incident has `last_drilled` within 90 days before `declared_at` (r-quarterly-drill).

example.note: Subject violations: the P1 matrix row omits the public status page, and the customer email and exec brief the row does list were never sent (r-severity-audience-matrix); the first post landed 48 minutes after declaration against a 15-minute deadline, with no next-update time (r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence); the component status contradicts the text and the Investigating post has no impact a customer can act on (r-status-page-lifecycle-states); the Investigating post names a database host and an unconfirmed cause (r-no-speculation-external); the commander is "team" and no actions are in flight (r-internal-post-fields); the exec brief is a 240-word technical narrative with "significant" for revenue and "soon" for ETA (r-exec-brief-one-screen); "resolved" with no window, scope, fix or postmortem date (r-resolution-and-postmortem-commitment); an unresolved token in a live post (r-placeholders-resolved-before-send); templates last drilled six months before the incident and a customer-email template with no next-update token (r-quarterly-drill, r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence).

antipattern.description: A matrix without a row for the declared severity, a highest-severity row without `status_page`, or `audiences_sent` that differs from the row.
antipattern.reason: r-severity-audience-matrix: "do we email customers?" is decided at 03:00 by whoever is on call.

antipattern.description: First external update after `first_post_deadline_minutes`, a gap between status-page updates longer than `update_interval_minutes`, or a non-Resolved update with no "next update by" line.
antipattern.reason: r-first-post-deadline-and-cadence: silence during an outage is read as abandonment.

antipattern.description: A status-page update without state, timestamp with timezone, impact or next-update time; states out of order; `component_status_matches_text` false.
antipattern.reason: r-status-page-lifecycle-states: "Operational" next to "checkout failing" teaches every reader that the page lies.

antipattern.description: External text with "we believe", "likely caused by", "appears to be", a vendor, person or host name, or any customer data before Resolved; any `review` flag true.
antipattern.reason: r-no-speculation-external: a retracted cause costs more trust than "we are investigating" ever would.

antipattern.description: An internal post whose commander or comms lead is not a named person, with no actions in flight, no incident link or no next checkpoint.
antipattern.reason: r-internal-post-fields: without a named commander two engineers restart the same service.

antipattern.description: An exec brief over 150 words, with `technical_narrative` true, a vague ETA, or impact without customers, revenue and SLA credits.
antipattern.reason: r-exec-brief-one-screen: three paragraphs about connection pools produce a reply-all asking "so is it fixed?".

antipattern.description: A Resolved update without a `resolved` block, or one missing start and end with timezone, scope, fix or a dated postmortem commitment; a post-incident email after the matrix deadline.
antipattern.reason: r-resolution-and-postmortem-commitment: every customer computes their own downtime for the SLA claim.

antipattern.description: Any filled text containing a double-brace token or a template comment, or a template body using a token outside `token_list`.
antipattern.reason: r-placeholders-resolved-before-send: it is the one comms failure customers screenshot.

antipattern.description: A template used for an incident whose `last_drilled` is more than 90 days before `declared_at`.
antipattern.reason: r-quarterly-drill: the retired component is found at minute 12 of a real P1.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
The four-template bundle and the severity matrix in Markdown, with the same tokens and fields.
